title: Where .NET is today
cards/0/body:
Servers and cloud: ASP.NET Core, on Linux and in containers.
Desktop: WPF and WinForms (Windows), Avalonia and MAUI (cross-platform).
Browser: Blazor on WebAssembly.
Games: Unity (Mono and IL2CPP, moving to CoreCLR), Godot 4 on .NET.
CAD and BIM: plugins for Revit, AutoCAD, Navisworks.
cards/1/body:
Up to and including version 2024, Revit and AutoCAD ran on .NET Framework 4.8. Since 2025 they run on .NET 8.

So a plugin for both eras means two builds: net48 and net8.0-windows. Future host versions will follow new LTS releases. To learn the runtime of a specific version, check the "What's New" notes for its API.
cards/2/task: Find the year Revit and AutoCAD moved to .NET 8.
cards/3/task: A plugin for Revit 2024 and Revit 2025: give each one its native build.
cards/4/q: Why can't a Revit 2025 plugin just stay on net48?
cards/4/options/0: Revit 2025 runs on .NET 8. A Framework build might load with caveats at best and can crash on missing APIs
cards/4/explain: Autodesk explicitly requires plugins to be rebuilt for .NET 8.
cards/5/q: Match each task to a technology
cards/6/q: Where does C# run today? Select all that apply.
cards/7/explain: Godot 4 moved to modern .NET, unlike Godot 3, which used Mono.
